classification.difficultyReason: Uses an algebraic complement calculation for two tickets among distinct prize-winning tickets.

content.prompt: If you hold two tickets in a lottery for which $n$ tickets were sold and 5 prizes are to be given, what is the probability that you will win at least one prize?

answer.short:
$\frac{10(n-3)}{n(n-1)}$, for integer $n\geq5$.

Use the complement that neither ticket wins.
answer.worked:
Take the five prizes to go to five distinct tickets, all winning-ticket sets being equally likely. There are $n-5$ losing tickets.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{neither ticket wins})&=\frac{n-5}{n}\times\frac{n-6}{n-1}\\P(\text{at least one prize})&=1-\frac{(n-5)(n-6)}{n(n-1)}\\P(\text{at least one prize})&=\frac{n(n-1)-(n-5)(n-6)}{n(n-1)}\\P(\text{at least one prize})&=\frac{10(n-3)}{n(n-1)}\end{align*}$$
For $n=5$, every ticket wins, so the probability is 1, also given by the final formula.
